problem.concept: Accurate prediction of GEBVs is a central and recurring challenge in plant and animal breeding.

The existence of a bewildering array of approaches for predicting breeding values using markers underscores the importance of identifying approaches able to efficiently and accurately predict breeding values.

task.concept: predicting GEBV using dense SNP markers.

contribution.concept: quantitative trait: dataset on 3000 progenies of 20 sires and 200 dams: simulated for the QTL-MAS 2011 workshop. The regression models were trained with a subset of 2000 phenotyped and genotyped individuals and used to predict GEBVs for the remaining 1000 progenies without phenotypes. The elastic net, lasso, adaptive lasso and the adaptive elastic net all had similar accuracies but outperformed ridge regression and ridge regression BLUP in terms of the Pearson correlation between predicted GEBVs and the true genomic value as well as the root mean squared error.
dataset: simulated for the QTL-MAS 2011 workshop: The performance of RR-BLUP was also somewhat better than that of ridge regression.

dataset: simulated for the QTL-MAS 2011 workshop: The elastic net, lasso, adaptive lasso and the adaptive elastic net all had similar accuracies but outperformed ridge regression and ridge regression BLUP in terms of the Pearson correlation between predicted GEBVs and the true genomic value as well as the root mean squared error. This pattern was replicated by the Pearson correlation between predicted GEBVs and the true breeding values (TBV) and the root mean squared error calculated with respect to TBV, except that accuracy was lower for all models, most especially for the adaptive elastic net.

dataset: simulated for the QTL-MAS 2011 workshop: The elastic net, lasso, adaptive lasso and the adaptive elastic net all had similar accuracies but outperformed ridge regression and ridge regression BLUP in terms of the Pearson correlation between predicted GEBVs and the true genomic value as well as the root mean squared error. The correlation between the predicted GEBV and simulated phenotypic values based on the fivefold CV also revealed a similar pattern except that the adaptive elastic net had lower accuracy than both the ridge regression methods.

ridge regression, ridge regression BLUP, lasso, adaptive lasso, elastic net and adaptive elastic net: All the six models had relatively high prediction accuracies for the simulated data set. Accuracy was higher for the lasso type methods than for ridge regression and ridge regression BLUP.

problem.concept: tests whose p-values cannot be computed explicitly but can be approximated using Monte Carlo simulation.

task.concept: obtaining the same rejections and non-rejections as the ones obtained if the p-values for all hypotheses had been available.

method.concept: generic algorithm for a general multiple testing procedure.

contribution.concept: Monte Carlo simulation: framework: generic algorithm for a general multiple testing procedure.
We establish conditions which guarantee that the rejections and non-rejections obtained through Monte Carlo simulations are identical to the ones obtained with the p-values.

generic algorithm for a general multiple testing procedure: Our framework is applicable to a general class of step-up and step-down procedures which includes many established multiple testing corrections such as the ones of Bonferroni, Holm, Sidak, Hochberg or Benjamini-Hochberg.

framework: generic algorithm for a general multiple testing procedure: show how to use our framework to improve algorithms available in the literature in such a way as to yield theoretical guarantees on their results. These modifications can easily be implemented in practice and lead to a particular way of reporting multiple testing results as three sets together with an error bound on their correctness, demonstrated exemplarily using a real biological dataset.
